newsitem.title: UK: S&P cuts ratings of four UK cable companies.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts ratings of four UK cable companies.

text.p: Standard & Poor's rating agency said on Thursday it had cut the ratings of Telewest Communications Plc, NTL Inc, Diamond Cable Communications Plc, and Comcast UK Cable Partners Ltd.

"The rating actions largely reflect S&P's view that industry fundamentals have weakened since the first ratings were assigned in 1994, and this has impacted the financial prospects of the sector over the medium to longer term," the agency said in a statement.
Telewest Communications' credit rating was lowered to BB minus from BB plus, and its senior unsecured rating to B plus from BB.
NTL's corporate rating was cut to B from B plus, and the senior unsecured rating was lowered to B minus from B.
Comcast was cut to B from B plus, and its senior unsecured rating was lowered to B minus from B.
Diamond Cable was lowered to B from B plus, and its senior unsecured debt was affirmed at B minus.
S&P said the outlook for all the companies was stable.
The agency said in a statement that consumer acceptance of cable and telephony services had so far been mixed.

It said there were "formidable competitive pressures" both from existing television and telecommunications companies, as well as from the future digital terrestrial television (DTT) which is contributing to confusion among consumers.
"Over the next few years, debt levels relative to cash flow generation are expected to remain extremely high," S&P said.
However, the agency said that DTT, as well as increasing competition, may increase general awareness of the pay television market, and spur growth.
"Planned cable offerings...appear superior to planned DTT offerings and may not require an initial capital outlay by the consumer," S&P said.
There was also the possibility that industry consolidation would offer economies of scale, for those operators strong enough to make acquisitions.

Cable operators were also well positioned to offer a variety of new, higher margin services such as high speed internet access "which would enable companies to broaden their revenues and cash flow source over the longer term," S&P added.
